rationale: Base station storage was at 98% with loop recording disabled, triggering error E-402 and preventing new events from being recorded. All devices were online and live view worked, ruling out network/peripheral faults. Enabling Loop Recording resolved the issue, confirming the root cause was storage full rather than failing memory.

repair_steps: Confirm with customer that new events are now being recorded after enabling Loop Recording.

output.customer_reply: We've resolved the issue by enabling Loop Recording on your base station. New events are now saving normally. If you'd like to keep all clips, you can export important ones and format storage. Let us know if you need further help!

args.action: In the app, go to Base Station Settings > Storage and enable Loop Recording. This will automatically overwrite the oldest clips when storage is full, so the E-402 warning stops recurring. (If the customer prefers to keep all clips, they can instead export important clips and then format the storage.)

results.text: Base station storage at or above 98 percent with loop recording disabled. Frontline action: enable loop recording or format storage.

Event clips are stored on the base station's internal eMMC (HB-100: 16 GB, HB-200: 32 GB). When loop recording is disabled and storage reaches 98 percent, new events are not recorded and error E-402 is shown. Enable loop recording in Base Station Settings > Storage, or format the storage after exporting clips.

Solid blue: online and connected to cloud. Blinking blue: pairing mode (lasts 120 seconds). Solid red: no internet uplink. Blinking red: booting or firmware update in progress, do not unplug. Solid purple: storage almost full (over 95 percent).
